name: Guyana
summary: Guyana taxes residents on worldwide income at 25% and 35% (35% above GYD 3,360,000 in 2026). Capital gains on assets held over 12 months bear a separate 20% capital gains tax, but gains on shares in public companies are exempt (whether this covers foreign listed shares is unconfirmed). Dividends from Guyanese companies are exempt; foreign dividends are ordinary income. No inheritance, estate, gift or wealth tax, and individuals have been exempt from property tax since 2025.

regimes.name: Ordinary tax residence
regimes.description: Worldwide income tax at 25%/35%; separate 20% capital gains tax; no inheritance, gift or wealth taxes.
regimes.eligibility: Resident if present more than 183 days in a year, residing permanently, or intending to reside permanently (PwC Residence).

capital_gains.summary: Capital gains tax of 20% applies to net gains from a change of ownership of assets by an individual; gains on assets disposed of within 12 months are taxed as income (up to 35%). Gains on the disposal of shares in public companies are exempt. A private residence is exempt if the proceeds are reinvested in another residence.

capital_gains.rate_basis: PwC Other taxes: 20% CGT on net gains (assets held over 12 months); exemption for shares in public companies (applied to Guyanese listed shares). Unlisted company shares and local real estate: 20%.
capital_gains.holding_period_rules: Assets disposed of within 12 months: gain taxed as income at 25%/35%.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Trading gains are business income at 25%/35%.
open_questions: Whether 'public companies' in the exemption include foreign listed companies, and whether CGT reaches foreign assets of residents, is not confirmed; listed_securities_foreign is null.
Capital Gains Tax Act text not opened.

dividends.summary: Dividends paid by resident companies to resident individuals are exempt. Foreign dividends are part of worldwide income taxed at 25% and 35% (top rate above GYD 3,360,000 chargeable income in 2026). Foreign tax credit is provided for income from an office, employment or profits and under treaties (Canada, UK, CARICOM, UAE).

dividends.rate_basis: Top PIT rate 35% (2026 threshold GYD 3,360,000) on foreign dividends; domestic dividends exempt (PwC Income determination).
dividends.withholding_outbound: 20% WHT on dividends to non-residents (treaty: Canada 15%, UK 10%, CARICOM 0%).
dividends.treaty_network: Treaties only with Canada, UK, UAE and CARICOM states.
open_questions: PwC mentions foreign income 'chargeable to Guyana tax on a remittance basis' without saying who qualifies; a remittance basis for non-domiciled residents may exist but was not confirmed.
Whether the unilateral credit covers foreign dividends is unclear; scored as 'none' (treaty relief only).

wealth_tax.summary: No net wealth tax; individuals are exempt from property tax from 2025.

sources.title: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries: Guyana - Individual - Other taxes

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Property Tax Act no longer applies to individuals from the 2025 year of income. Stamp duty on conveyances and share transfers.

inheritance.summary: Guyana does not impose inheritance, estate or gift taxes.

sources.title: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries: Guyana - Individual - Other taxes

inheritance.important_exceptions: Stamp duty applies to deeds of conveyance; probate costs not researched.

residency.tax_residency_test: More than 183 days in a year, permanent residence, or intention to reside permanently; 'ordinarily resident' = habitually resident (PwC Residence).

routes.name: Residence permit
routes.requirements: CARICOM nationals have facilitated entry; others need a residence permit. Not researched.

corporate.summary: 25% for non-commercial companies; 40% for commercial companies (minimum tax 2% of turnover); 45% telecoms.
